title: User research still matters in the age of AI
description: AI can analyze interviews, but it doesn't live the experience. Why research with real people is still essential, and how AI and research complement each other.

related.title: Clint Intelligence
related.body: In practice: AI agents that act inside the CRM and keep the person in control.

blocks.text: So a question keeps coming up more and more:
If AI can do all of that, do we still need to talk to real users?
My answer is yes.
And research might be getting even more important.
AI can analyze. But it doesn't live the experience.

data.ai: An AI can help transcribe them, organize them and find recurring themes in a few minutes.
data.saves: That saves a lot of time.
data.diff: But there's a difference between reading a transcript and being there during a conversation.
data.notice: When you watch someone trying to use a product, some things just don't show up in the text.
cues: The way they try to explain a problem
data.context: A sentence that seems simple can mean a lot more when you know the context it was said in.

blocks.text: The problem with answers that are too perfect
AI is really good at organizing information.
And that can also be a problem.
When we turn research into a summary too quickly, we can lose the messy parts.
The contradictions.
The exceptions.
The stories that don't fit into a category.
But those are exactly the parts that often spark a good design question.
Imagine eight people show the same behavior.
It's easy to turn that into an insight.
But maybe a ninth person does something completely different.
That ninth person might reveal a need we hadn't noticed yet.
That's why research shouldn't just be about looking for patterns.
It's also important to notice what doesn't fit.

blocks.caption: The summary groups the people who are alike. The one who doesn't fit may reveal the next design question.

blocks.text: AI can help a lot with research
That doesn't mean leaving AI aside.
Quite the opposite.
We can use AI to:

items: turn findings into questions for new research.

blocks.text: The time savings can be huge.
But I'd set one simple rule:
Use AI to speed up research, not to replace contact with reality.
Synthetic users are not real users
You can ask an AI to play the role of a certain profile.

blocks.caption: An answer that's too perfect is a red flag.

data.prompt: “Imagine you're a 35-year-old using a finance app for the first time.”
notes: The answer may sound very convincing
It isn't using its own money
lacks: It isn't afraid of losing a piece of information.
It isn't trying to do it in a hurry.
It isn't dealing with the reality of that context.
data.a: A simulation can help explore possibilities.
data.b: But it shouldn't be treated as evidence about real users.

blocks.text: Research also builds empathy within the team
There's another benefit of research we sometimes forget.
When a team sits in on a real interview, everyone learns.
Support recognizes problems that already show up in tickets.
Good research creates a shared language.
After hearing someone say:
“I didn't know if I could trust that information.”
It's much easier for the team to remember that problem when making a decision.
That shared learning is hard to replace with a report.
The researcher's role is changing too
With AI helping with operational tasks, research work can shift to other activities.
More time to:

items: assess the quality of the evidence.

blocks.text: Less manual work doesn't mean less research.
It can mean more room to do better research.
Not every decision needs a huge research project
Doing research doesn't necessarily mean spending weeks on interviews.
Sometimes we just need to answer one specific question.
For example:
“Do people understand this message?”
A quick test can help.
Or:
“Why is there so much drop-off at this step?”
We can combine analytics with a few interviews.
Or:
“Which of these solutions is easier to understand?”
A usability test may be enough to find problems.
Research needs to be connected to the decision.
The right question isn't “AI or research?”
Maybe the question is:

blocks.caption: AI and research don't compete: they play different roles.

blocks.text: “How can we use AI to do better research?”
We can spend less time organizing files and more time talking to users.
We can analyze more interviews.
We can compare more information.
We can find questions we hadn't noticed.
We can test hypotheses faster.
But we need to keep going to the source.
Because the real user doesn't exist inside our model.
They exist outside of it.
The future of research can be faster, not less human
I believe AI can make research more accessible for small teams and speed up many steps of the process.
But that doesn't mean abandoning the fundamentals.
Research still needs a good question.
It needs context.
It needs real people when we're trying to understand real people.
It needs interpretation.
And it needs to be connected to a decision.

data.lead: In the end, we can use AI to analyze thousands of answers.
data.lead2: But we still need to know:
questions: What are we trying to find out?
Which decision depends on this learning?
data.last: What will we do differently after learning this?
